clue.text: Deeply dejected at her, conceivably?

indicators.note: conceivably says the clue words could have come about through some process, which the answer read as an instruction describes

parts.note: the two words 'at her' are what you get when a certain vital organ is smashed and its letters put back in another order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the person they were snubbed by left them feeling very low.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'conceivably' and the question mark flag that the answer, read as an instruction, describes how 'at her' came about.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose heart is broken is overwhelmed with grief, deeply downcast.

clue.text: Stand up and embrace restaurant employee I sacked

parts.note: to embrace someone is to hold them

indicators.note: sacked means dismissed, so the letter for I is thrown out of the word

parts.note: a waiter serves at tables in a restaurant

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get up and hug a waiter who has just been fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand up' is used in the sense of an argument surviving scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument that will stand up, or hold water, is sound and survives testing; the idiom comes from a vessel that does not leak.

clue.text: Release verse flipping graduate alone pens

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the graduate's letters are read backwards

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the word for alone holds the abbreviation for verse

parts.note: sole means alone, single

explanation.surface: A graduate on their own writes poetry and lets it go.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to free them from blame or obligation.

clue.text: Set of exam questions in part Pete's composed

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of 'part Pete's' are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Pete has written part of an examination himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A test paper is the printed sheet of questions candidates answer in an exam.

clue.text: Chicken sheds cold for this bird

indicators.note: sheds means casts off, so the cowardly word loses its letter for cold

parts.note: chicken means cowardly, as craven does
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A hen moults in the cold, turning into another kind of bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Current hospital vehicle Jack's regularly seen around city

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word Jack's

explanation.surface: Jack keeps seeing an electric ambulance driving about town.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of 'Jack's' gives AK; 'around' turns the whole run I-H-CAR-AK backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Karachi is Pakistan's largest city and main port.

clue.text: One man repeatedly discovered this person's innocent

indicators.note: discovered means stripped of covering, done repeatedly to each word, so only the middle letters of 'One' and 'man' remain

parts.note: this person's, read as 'this person has', gives I've, with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone protests their innocence after a man keeps being found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the speaker, I, so 'this person's' is 'I have', shortened to I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means unworldly and guileless, lacking experience of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Boarding ship, key sailors with experience

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the key goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, stands for a ship
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Seasoned crewmen climb aboard a vessel carrying a key.
explanation.definitionFit: Old salts are veteran seamen who have spent years at sea.

clue.text: Back initially clever young woman for such post

parts.note: to back a proposal is to second it, support it

indicators.note: initially means taking only the opening letter of the word clever

parts.note: a lass is a young woman

explanation.surface: A bright girl is asked to support some kind of job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a job, but it is mail: second-class post is the slower UK postal rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-class is the cheaper, slower tier of British mail delivery, as opposed to first-class.

clue.text: Monarch, character inspiring past legends essentially

indicators.note: inspiring is read as breathing in, so the symbol takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a sign is a character or symbol
over means past or finished

indicators.note: essentially means the heart of the word legends, its middle letter

explanation.surface: A king is a figure who brings old tales to life.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is a king or queen, the supreme ruler of a state.

clue.text: Wind Ron up over son filling US playhouse

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read upwards, so Ron's letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: filling means stuffing, so the abbreviation for son goes inside the playhouse

parts.note: theater is the American spelling of theatre

explanation.surface: Ron winds up his son, who is in a play at an American theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link word: in a down clue the reversed name sits over the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A north-easter is a wind or gale blowing from the north-east.

clue.text: Bloomer, mistake by Conservative that is painful

parts.note: ow is the cry that says something hurts
a slip is a mistake

explanation.surface: A Tory politician makes a gaffe that hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, matching 'mistake', but it is a flower, something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow wild flower of the primrose family, so it blooms.

clue.text: Doubtful when advancing new form of energy

indicators.note: advancing means moving forward, so a letter of the word for doubtful is shifted towards the front

parts.note: doubtful means uncertain, unclear

explanation.surface: A new kind of power is uncertain as it develops.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear power comes from splitting or fusing atoms, one kind of energy.

clue.text: Excerpt from publication, it represents maybe explosive content

indicators.note: Excerpt from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A quoted passage from a magazine is said to stand for something incendiary.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a component of gunpowder, so it may be in an explosive.

clue.text: Father in bed after taking run, feeling back

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the garden bed word

parts.note: a patch is a bed in a garden

indicators.note: back means reversed, so the run and the feeling are read from the end
after taking says the feeling follows once the run has been taken first

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an air is a feeling or impression about something

explanation.surface: Dad is in bed after a jog, his back aching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after taking' sets the run first and the feeling after it; 'back' turns that pair round before it goes into the garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is the male head of a family or tribe, a father figure.

clue.text: Woodland plants with clear shapes, according to Spooner

indicators.note: according to Spooner signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words, after the Rev. Spooner

parts.note: free means clear, as in a road clear of traffic
turns means shapes, as wood is shaped on a lathe

explanation.surface: Forest plants grow in neat, distinct forms.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of FREE TURNS gives TREE FURNS, spelt as the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree ferns are large ferns with trunk-like stems that grow in forests.

clue.text: Considered again if temperature is below summer average ultimately

indicators.note: is below in a down clue places the condition and temperature under the final letters
ultimately means the final letter of each of the words summer and average

parts.note: though can mean if, as in 'as though'

explanation.surface: A forecaster reconsiders when the heat falls short of the summer norm.
explanation.definitionFit: To rethink something is to reconsider it and form a fresh view.

clue.text: Drawing equine, artist Charlie recalled others being excited

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the artist and Charlie are written backwards

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: being excited means stirred up, so the letters of 'others' are mixed

explanation.surface: An artist remembers a sketch of a horse that stirred up the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' looks like a sketch, but it means pulling: a horse that hauls carts.
explanation.definitionFit: A carthorse is a heavy, strong horse bred for pulling loads.

clue.text: Rider perhaps looking very tired and gaunt

definitions.meaning: Henry Rider ... was the author of King Solomon's Mines, so Rider is an example of one of that surname
worn, hollow-cheeked and exhausted in appearance

explanation.definitionFit: H. Rider Haggard was a Victorian adventure novelist; separately, the adjective describes a drawn, exhausted face.

clue.text: Old man adopting diet ate occasionally leavened bread

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the father word holds the picked letters

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: occasionally means taking every other letter of 'diet ate'

explanation.surface: Dad goes on a diet but sometimes eats some bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, slightly leavened Middle Eastern bread that opens into a pocket.

clue.text: Dish put on gold table

parts.note: a plate is a dish
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A dish is set down on a golden table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table' here is the flat raised land, a tableland.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an area of high, level ground, also called a tableland.

clue.text: Specifies indications of arsenic poisoning?

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
signs are indications

explanation.surface: A doctor lists the symptoms of someone given arsenic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'poisoning?' are link material: the question mark flags that the 'symptoms' are just the symbol As plus signs.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign something is to allot or designate it, which is specifying it.

clue.text: Assumes Oscar wears revolutionary headband

indicators.note: wears means has on, so the reversed word carries the letter for Oscar inside
revolutionary is read as turning round, so the word for assumes runs backwards

parts.note: dons means puts on, assumes as clothing
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man takes on the look of a rebel by putting on a band round his head.
explanation.definitionFit: A snood is a band or net worn to hold back the hair.

clue.text: Bargain with Liberal leader finally reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the name is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: David Steel was the final leader of the Liberal Party before it merged into the Liberal Democrats in 1988

explanation.surface: A politician's last deal is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: The UK Liberal Party merged with the SDP in 1988; its leader at the end was David Steel.
explanation.definitionFit: A steal is something bought at a very low price, a real bargain.

clue.text: Using every effort, even abroad

parts.note: flat means even, level
out means abroad, away from home

explanation.surface: Someone tries their hardest even when overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Working flat-out means at full speed, giving maximum effort.

clue.text: Invent catchphrases galore, mostly seen broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are sown in a new order
mostly means most of the word galore, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A copywriter coins many slogans that are then heard on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloganeer is someone who devises slogans, so to sloganeer is to make up memorable phrases.

clue.text: Old king demanding English not American garden tool

indicators.note: English not American says the letter for English replaces the letter for American

parts.note: Edgar was a tenth-century king of England

explanation.surface: An ancient king insists on a British rather than US garden implement.
explanation.definitionFit: An edger is a tool for trimming the edges of a lawn.

clue.text: Daughter having hunch about drunk at first going: "Trump's nothing"

indicators.note: at first going means the opening letter of the word for drunk is lost

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk
to hunch down is to squat

explanation.surface: A daughter suspects a drunk is saying the President has no hand to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump's' is surface dressing for the US president; diddly-squat is American slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Diddly-squat is US slang meaning absolutely zero, not a thing.
